svg.title: Possible anaphylaxis five-minute and follow-up action card
svg.desc: Anaphylaxis follow-up card. Five minutes after the first adrenaline device, if severe signs have not improved, are still present or have returned, use the person's next adrenaline device, following their current action plan and that device's own instructions. Follow any directions from Triple Zero and record the device and time. If no device is available, call Triple Zero immediately, use the correct position and watch breathing; there is no first-aid substitute. Prevent further contact only when safe and without delaying care. For known asthma and known severe allergy, give adrenaline first after possible contact with that severe allergen, then follow the asthma plan. Keep watching response and breathing, start CPR if unresponsive and not breathing normally, and continue ambulance and hospital care even after improvement.
svg.text: ANAPHYLAXIS — KEEP GOING
Five-minute check and continued care
WARNING — WORKING CARDS; NOT DEVICE TRAINING
Subjective estimates: core source match 95%; new layout 60%.
These are not safety, treatment-success or survival probabilities.
This card does not choose a device or dose. Follow the person’s
current plan, exact device instructions and 000. Allergy-clinical,
device, practical and stressed-reader review is outstanding.
FIVE MINUTES AFTER FIRST DEVICE
Severe signs not better, still there or back?
Use the person’s next adrenaline device.
Follow their current plan and that device’s
own instructions. Follow any directions from 000.
Record the device and time.
NO ADRENALINE DEVICE?
Call 000 immediately. Keep the person safely positioned, watch
breathing and follow the call-taker. There is no first-aid substitute.
Prevent further contact only if safe; never delay care.
ASTHMA + KNOWN SEVERE ALLERGY
Sudden severe breathing trouble after possible contact
with something they are severely allergic to?
Give adrenaline first, then follow the asthma plan.
Reliever, antihistamine or plant remedy does not replace it.
KEEP STILL AND KEEP WATCHING
• recheck response and normal breathing continuously
• unresponsive AND not breathing normally: start CPR
• unresponsive but breathing normally: use Card 2
• do not cancel help or allow walking after improvement
• ambulance and hospital care are still required
CARE COMES FIRST
Reading, recording and supplies must not delay
adrenaline, 000 or CPR.
WORKING DRAFT — use with Cards 1 and 2; follow 000
